page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with the running head at the top and a catchword at the bottom right. In the lower part of the text block the lines are centred and narrowed, but they continue the same paragraph. No margin notes.

main_text.p: rifmo quadragefimoquarto, & quinto,Se-ctionis quartæ. Quos febres longæ exer-cent(inquir)ijs tubercula ad articulos, vel labores fiunt:& mox,quibus tubercula,vel in articulis labores post febres fiunt, ijs cibarijs pluribus utuntur. At huiusmodi febres absq; aliquo viscere male affecto fieri non posse, apud omnes medicos est in consenso:quod sane ostendit Fernelius libro de Febribus, ubi intermittentium caufas tradit. Tunc enim ab hepate, & venis in articulos fit fluxio,cum huiusmodi partes tanta grauatur copia,ut eam nec excipere, nec continere queant: idcirco per emissaria ad exteriores partes hos supervacaneos humores propellunt, ubi ob musculorum laxitatem nullum excitant dolorem, hinc verò in articulos, ubi ob adstrictionem partium retinentur. Quoniam autem ibi sensiles partes, ut ligamenta, distendunt,idcirco his partib. dolores cientur[?].

page.notes: Catchword "EXER-" is at the bottom right. A small mark "R" stands to its left; it is probably a printer's mark and is not transcribed. "hinc ue / rò": the word is split at the line end without a printed hyphen, so it is written whole as "verò". "fesso" in the printed text has been read as "fenso" in "consenso"; the first letters of the word are split across the lines, so the reading is uncertain. Last word "cientur": the reading is doubtful and may be incomplete.
